strings.name: Carlos Alcaraz
strings.role: Tennis player · Career Grand Slam winner
strings.summary: Born in Murcia, Alcaraz entered professional tennis as a teenager and developed a game built on speed, attacking forehands and net play. His 2022 US Open title made him the youngest No.1 in ATP rankings history. After titles at Wimbledon and Roland-Garros, he won the 2026 Australian Open to complete the career Grand Slam at twenty-two. He returned from a wrist injury to win more titles later that year.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected career milestones; results and records refer to their cited dates, not an exhaustive results log or live ranking.
strings.influence.rationale: A young major champion and world No.1 representing a new generation in men's tennis.

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Completed the set of four major singles titles at the 2026 Australian Open, aged 22 years and 272 days.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Youngest ATP No.1
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Reached No.1 at nineteen after the 2022 US Open and finished that season at the top.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: First Paris Masters title
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Beat Ben Shelton 7–6, 7–5 for his first Paris Masters title, continuing his successful return from a wrist injury.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Australian Open completed the Slam set
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Defeated Novak Djokovic to win his seventh major and complete the career Grand Slam at 22 years and 272 days.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: French Open and US Open titles
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Beat Jannik Sinner in both major finals and finished the year at No.1 for a second time.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Olympic singles silver
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Won singles silver in Paris after losing to Djokovic; also played doubles with Rafael Nadal.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: French Open–Wimbledon double
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Followed his first French Open title by defending Wimbledon against Djokovic, taking his major total to four.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: First Wimbledon title
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Beat Djokovic in a five-set final for his second major, ending the Serbian’s long Wimbledon winning streak.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: US Open champion and No.1
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Won his first major at the US Open and became the youngest No.1 in ATP rankings history.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: First tour title in Umag
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Won his first ATP Tour singles title in Umag, Croatia, at eighteen.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Won on his ATP Tour debut
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Made his ATP Tour debut in Rio at sixteen and defeated Albert Ramos-Vinolas.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Turned professional
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Began his professional career as a teenager, progressing from Spain’s development system and lower-level events.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Born in El Palmar
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Born into a tennis family in Murcia; his father coached and managed a club.
